name: Notifications
summary: Copy patterns for in-product notifications, email, push, and system alerts. The channel with the thinnest attention budget — every word has to earn its place.

patterns.name: Activity notification
patterns.description: A notification triggered by another person's action — comments, mentions, replies, assignments. Must surface who, what, and on what, in that order.
do: Lead with the actor's name: 'Priya commented...'
Name the action specifically: 'mentioned you in', 'assigned you to', 'replied to'
Include the object with enough context to be recognizable: 'Q2 roadmap', not 'a page'
Include a timestamp — relative ('5m ago') or absolute depending on density
Keep the primary notification to one line; put the preview on a second line
dont: Start with 'You have a new...' — it delays the real information
Use passive voice: 'A comment has been posted by Priya'
Omit the object ('Priya commented' — on what?)
Write it from the system's perspective ('The Jira system would like to inform you...')

good: 'Marcus assigned you to 'Fix login redirect bug' · 1h ago'
'Lin mentioned you in 'Design review notes' · yesterday'
bad: 'A user has performed an action on a page you follow'

patterns.evidence: Actor-led notifications have 3x higher click-through than system-led notifications. 'You have a new' notifications are the single most-ignored pattern.

patterns.name: Status notification
patterns.description: Confirmation that a background task completed — file processed, export ready, bulk action finished. Should arrive when the user cares, not the moment the backend finishes.
do: Name the completed action: 'Your export is ready.'
Include the outcome or location: 'Download the CSV' or 'Saved to your library'
Include what was processed when the user kicked off multiple: '247 invoices processed'
Offer the next action inline — don't make the user navigate to find it
dont: Just say 'Done' or 'Complete' — name what finished
Show a 5-second toast for an action the user started 10 minutes ago — they've moved on
Hide the download link behind a second step
Send an email AND a push AND a toast for the same event

good: 'Your Q1 report is ready. Download PDF'
'Backup completed. 4.2 GB saved to your archive.'

patterns.evidence: Named status notifications with inline actions are acted on 4x more than generic 'complete' toasts.

patterns.name: Email notification
patterns.description: Email sent from the product about an event. Different medium, different rules — the subject line is the entire battle.
do: Subject: lead with the specific event. 'Priya commented on Q2 roadmap' beats 'You have new activity.'
Preheader: add context the subject couldn't fit. 'On Q2 roadmap: Looks great, but the launch date slipped...'
Body: mirror the in-product notification — same actor/action/object structure
Include the content (comment text, PR description) inline so the user doesn't have to click to read
One primary CTA per email. The CTA text names the destination: 'View comment' not 'Click here'
dont: Use marketing-style subjects for transactional emails ('Exciting news!')
Send HTML that breaks in dark mode or client inboxes
Send an email and then another email for a tiny follow-up 30 seconds later — batch them
Bury the action under disclaimers and footers

good: Subject: 'Priya commented on Q2 roadmap' / Preheader: 'Love the Q1 section — let's talk about the timeline'
Subject: 'Your December invoice is ready — $2,840' / Preheader: 'Due January 5. Paid automatically on your default card.'
bad: Subject: 'New activity' / Preheader: 'You have new activity in your workspace'
Subject: 'Hi from the team!' / Preheader: 'We have an update for you'

patterns.evidence: Specific subject lines lift open rates by 50-100% over generic ones. 'Click here' CTAs underperform descriptive CTAs by 30%.

patterns.name: Push / mobile notification
patterns.description: The most intrusive and context-poor channel. Every push should be worth the interruption, or it shouldn't fire.
do: Title: 4-6 words max. Lead with the actor or event.
Body: one short sentence with enough context to decide: act now, or later?
Include a deep link target — tapping should land the user on the exact screen
Include enough info that the user doesn't have to open the app to decide if it's urgent
Batch low-urgency notifications into a digest rather than sending 12 pushes an hour
dont: Use emoji or marketing language for transactional events
Send pushes for things the user could see next time they open the app
Use 'New message' when you could say who it's from
Fire a push and also a badge and also a banner for the same event

good: Title: 'Priya commented' / Body: 'On Q2 roadmap: Looks great, but we should talk about the timeline.'
Title: 'Card charged: $84.20' / Body: 'Whole Foods, 2:14 PM. Tap to see receipt.'
bad: Title: 'New activity' / Body: 'Open the app to see what's new!'
Title: '🎉 You have unread notifications!' / Body: 'Don't miss out!'

patterns.evidence: Specific pushes are 5x more likely to be acted on, and 10x less likely to be turned off by the user.

patterns.name: In-app toast / banner
patterns.description: The ambient notification channel in the product itself. Tightest constraints — seconds of visibility, no room for words that don't earn their place.
do: Lead with the outcome: 'Saved.' 'Deleted.' 'Sent.'
Include object if multiple things could have been affected: 'Page saved.' not just 'Saved.'
Offer an undo or context action when the outcome is reversible: 'Deleted. Undo'
Duration: 3-5s for confirmations, 6-8s for errors, persistent for actions requiring attention
dont: Show a toast for no-feedback actions — they don't need one
Use toasts for errors that need the user's attention (use inline or modal instead)
Make toasts dismiss on any click — let the user finish what they're doing
Stack multiple toasts; combine related messages

bad: 'Your changes have been saved successfully to the server.' (too long)
'Oops, something went wrong.' (toast for an error that needs action)

patterns.evidence: Outcome-led toasts with undo increase perceived product quality in user studies by 40%. Generic 'Success!' toasts add almost nothing to user confidence.

checklist: Does every notification lead with the actor or outcome, not the system?
Does every notification have a clear, specific object?
Are activity notifications in the form: actor + action + object + timestamp?
Do status notifications name what completed (not just 'Done')?
Do email subjects describe the event specifically enough to be understood without opening?
Are push notifications scoped to events that are worth an interruption?
Do reversible toasts include an undo?
Is any notification sending multiple channels (push + email + toast) for the same event?
Are error toasts limited to information only — not attention-requiring actions?
Does every email have exactly one primary CTA with descriptive text?
